claim: The app-managed relay can issue bounded operator-clock-expiring v3 bearer invitations and rotate or recover an active member under an exact registry revision while invalidating every previous capability copy, preserving v2 and legacy compatibility.
commands: node ../scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm exec -- vitest run src/workspace/websocketProjectInvite.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectProvider.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectStore.test.ts src/migrations.test.ts src/workspace/WorkspaceView.ui.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectProductFlow.integration.test.ts
proved: Native issue and rotation accept no expiry or 300 through 31,536,000 seconds; invalid or overflowing lifetime input fails before the registry save.
Authorization denies a member at and after its stored expiresAtMs before a protected room frame is sent.
Exact-revision rotation preserves member ID and role, increments capabilityGeneration, replaces expiry, stores only the replacement SHA-256 digest, and never returns the old capability.
The owned relay restarts after rotation so the old capability is denied and the replacement reconnects to the retained Yjs document.
Store v6 and managed-v3 invitations strictly persist and disclose generation plus a JavaScript-Date-representable expiry; managed-v2 and legacy-v1 invitations remain readable.

The host product offers bounded lifetime presets plus Rotate / recover, shows expiry/generation, presents the replacement invitation once, and replaces its own persisted access when rotating the current member.
notProved: Trusted time: expiry uses the relay host operating-system clock and can be affected by clock rollback or operator control.
Automatic or authenticated replacement delivery; the relay operator must send the newly shown invitation through a separate channel.
Resistance while a valid invitation is copied; every holder retains the same authority until expiry, rotation, or revocation.
Human identity, signed device-to-role binding, shared or remote membership administration, participant-controlled recovery, or key escrow.
Public TLS/WSS operation, encrypted update logs, independent backup/restore, hostile-frame fuzzing, five-client soak, or physical packaged two-install interaction.
